mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real rates remain negative.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
